description: Published poets from Kent and Sussex come together at this year’s Festival with readings of their work followed by a short open mic set. Hosted by Christopher Horton. Poets include John McCullough, Setareh Ebrahimi, Bethany Goodwill, Carolyn Oulton, David Dykes and Mat Ritches. Headliner: John McCullough John McCullough’s book of poems, Reckless Paper Birds (Penned in the Margins) won the 2020 Hawthornden Prize for Literature as well as being shortlisted for the Costa Poetry Award. John’s collections have been Books of the Year for publications including The Guardian, The Times, The Independent and The Telegraph and he also won the Polari First Book Prize. His fifth collection, Crowd Voltage , was published in March 2026 by Bloodaxe. Other readings from: David Dykes is a poet and host and co-organiser of the Medway poetry night Big Trouble. David has produced three chapbooks including Haunt Me! Haunt Me! Do It Again! about Gillingham-based cult leader James Jershom Jezreel and has been featured in Confluence and The Menteur . He is currently part of the Southbank Centre's 2026-27 New Poets Collective and taking part in their Poet in Every Port project. Mat Riches is ITV’s unofficial poet-in-residence. Recent work has appeared in Wild Court, The New Statesman, The Friday Poem and Finished Creatures . He co-runs Rogue Strands poetry evenings and has a pamphlet out with Red Squirrel Press. Bethany Goodwill is an artist, poet, and co-host of Rochester poetry night Big Trouble. Her work has been published in Confluence and The Menteur , and she has been described as "the greatest car-based poet of our times" and "a toad in women's clothing". She likes Earl Grey tea, cats, the winter, and spicy food. Carolyn Oulton is Professor of Victorian Literature and teaches on the Creative Writing BA at CCCU. title: Canterbury Choral Society presents Elgar: The Dream of Gerontius
description: This event is organised, managed and delivered by Canterbury Choral Society. Priority booking for Canterbury Choral Society Benefactors open on Wednesday 23 September 10am, Canterbury Choral Society Friends' priority booking will open on Wednesday 30 September 10am. Public sales open Wednesday 7 October 10am. This is the best of me; for the rest, I ate, and drank, and slept, loved, and hated, like another; my life was as the vapour, and is not; but this I saw and knew: this, if anything of mine, is worth your memory. So wrote Elgar, quoting Ruskin, on the final page of the score of The Dream of Gerontius . Many works followed, some of which, it could be argued, reached even greater heights, but Gerontius remains thoroughly Elgarian, filled with moments of touching, searing beauty and the majestic climaxes for which he is known. None is more powerful than its closing stages, sung by the Angel as Gerontius enters Heaven. At the moment when Gerontius ‘sees God’, there is a blinding and deafening flash of sound, with the entire orchestra instructed to play ‘for one moment’ at its fullest power. Come and hear for yourself in the glorious setting of Canterbury Cathedral. Canterbury Choral Society will be joined by the London Mozart Players and an outstanding team of soloists. title: Death of Gesualdo: Concert Theatre Works & The Gesualdo Six
description: World renowned vocal ensemble The Gesualdo Six bring the chilling music and biography of composer Carlo Gesualdo to life in an exceptional multi-media concert directed by Bill Barclay with choreography by Will Tuckett. Following the success of Secret Byrd, Death of Gesualdo sees The Gesualdo Six collaborate once more with Bill Barclay’s Concert Theatre Works to tell the story of troubled madrigalist Carlo Gesualdo (1566 – 1613). Gesualdo may be most famous for murdering his wife and her lover in bed, but among composers he is revered for anticipating chromaticism by 200 years. 'Six actors join the singers on stage to tell Gesualdo’s dark, troubled story through puppetry, dance and tableaux vivants reminiscent of Renaissance paintings to a score of some of Gesualdo’s darkest music, including Tenebrae (a mass for the composer’s own death), performed with the Gesualdo Six’s renowned “supreme precision".' description: Handle with Care is a theatre performance in a box. No actors, no technicians. Just a box. And you. A box is mailed to the theatre. They provide the structure; you shape the experience. Choose your role — take the lead or observe as others make choices that steer the performance in unexpected directions. Together, you create something special. For one hour, live something unique, fleeting, and unrepeatable. What is yours, stays yours. Take good care of it. And send them a postcard.
